meta.title: Use of generators to reduce memory usage via a LazyMultiSet
meta.body_summary: Introduce LazyMultiSet and generator-based lazy evaluation for d2mini operators to reduce memory usage; awaiting benchmark validation before merging.

perf_labels.notes: Cursor PR introducing generator-based lazy evaluation; reviewer approved code but requires performance benchmarks before merging.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 3399 changed lines, this is a large refactor by absolute volume, though a substantial amount of churn comes from added-then-removed analysis markdowns (net ~463 addition). The PR touches many operators in d2mini, representing a significant architectural change. It remains open pending benchmark validation.

review_details.concern_detail: Reviewer kevin-dp approved the implementation but explicitly required careful benchmarking of memory and execution performance before merging; inline comments also requested code simplifications and an additional test case for cancellation of multiplicities.
review_details.performance_claim: Using generators and LazyMultiSet reduces memory usage versus eager evaluation.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: Large‑scale operator refactor with generators crosses into performance territory where maintainers demand concrete benchmarks; Cursor provided the code but no performance validation.

detection_detail.code_reading: kevin-dp reviewed the code and questioned the overhead of LazyMultiSet in topK, requested deduplication of lazyJoin branches, and asked for an extra cancellation test case.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: PR body only states the intention to benchmark; no profiler results, tables, or numeric before/after data are provided.
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: PR is still open; author acknowledged the need for benchmarks and outlined a manual testing plan involving peak memory, execution time, and GC time.

core_change_summary.description: Added a LazyMultiSet class with generator-based map, filter, concat, consolidate, etc. Refactored operators (filter, map, negate, distinct, reduce, topK, topKWithFractionalIndex, consolidate, join, output) to use lazy generators and direct iteration. Added a lazyJoin generator in indexes. Removed an unnecessary constructor from NegateOperator. Updated existing tests and added new LazyMultiSet tests.
core_change_summary.secondary_note: Several analysis markdowns and a demo test file were added during the iteration and later removed; they do not affect the final implementation.
change_trajectory: Initial commit introduced LazyMultiSet and refactored basic operators.
Subsequent commits extended lazy support to all operators, added design analysis docs, and experimented with true lazy evaluation for complex operators (which was later reverted to pseudo‑lazy).
Further refactoring improved topK, consolidate, distinct, and reduce operators; a lazy join generator was added.
Cleanup commits removed unused documentation files, a demo test, and an unnecessary NegateOperator constructor.
Final commit added a type annotation in a test; PR was then reviewed and approved, but merge is blocked pending performance benchmarks.

review_signals.summary: Implementation LGTM but careful benchmarking of memory and performance is required before merging.
review_signals.action_taken: Author acknowledged and outlined a manual testing plan for peak memory, execution time, and GC time.

review_signals.summary: Requested removal of duplication between both branches in the lazyJoin generator.
Questioned overhead of creating a LazyMultiSet just to consolidate and then copy into an array in topK; suggested a direct consolidation loop.
Requested an additional test case for the scenario where multiplicities cancel out.
Author agreed with the need for benchmarks and proposed to measure peak memory, execution time, and GC time via manual browser‑based performance traces.

collaboration_trajectory: Cursor made 19 commits over two days, iterating on lazy evaluation from initial implementation to final cleanup.
Reviewer kevin-dp approved the code but emphasised the necessity of performance benchmarks.
Author samwillis agreed and detailed a three‑pronged testing strategy; no further commits were made as of the PR's current open state.
